title: Parts import with a blank Manufacturer keeps the part's manufacturer
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Needs: 1 user (Admin) · 1 browser · a spreadsheet program · about 20 minutes
  • Build: the Part Lifecycle QA build (no build exists yet; use the build named in the test run).
  • User: [Admin] = you, signed in with the Admin role, which by default has 'Part Library & Inventory → View / Create & Edit / Delete' and See Financial Data.
  • Location: [Loc-1] = the location picked in the top-bar location switcher at the start; every step runs at [Loc-1] unless it names another location.
  • Data: [Part-A] = tracked part with a manufacturer [Mfr-1] and Sell Price $20.00. [CSV-1] = an import file with one row for [Part-A], Manufacturer cell blank, Sell Price 26.00.
  • Names and numbers marked (e.g. …) are examples only. What must hold is the status (active or inactive), tracking, quantity and link described above.

Setup

  1. Go to Parts → Inventory, click "New Inventory Part" and fill in Description (e.g. ZZAUTOTEST PL IMPMFR PART), Part Number (e.g. ZZAUTOTEST-PL-IMPMFR-01), Category (e.g. Uncategorized), Cost (e.g. $10.00), Sell Price (e.g. $20.00), Manufacturer (pick the first manufacturer offered); leave "Track quantities and cost of goods" on; set the default bin's Quantity to 4; click Save.
  2. [Part-A] = the part number you typed (e.g. ZZAUTOTEST-PL-IMPMFR-01); [Desc-A] = the description you typed (e.g. ZZAUTOTEST PL IMPMFR PART).
  3. [Mfr-1] = the manufacturer you picked.
  4. Go to Settings → Data Import → Inventory and download the import template. Fill one row for [Part-A] with Part Number, Description, Category, Cost 10.00, Sell Price 26.00 and leave the Manufacturer cell empty; save as CSV. [CSV-1] = that file.
  5. Check the setup worked: [Part-A]'s dialog shows Manufacturer [Mfr-1]; the Manufacturer cell of [CSV-1] is empty.
custom_steps:
1. Go to Settings → Data Import → Inventory, upload [CSV-1] and run the import.
  2. Open [Part-A] on Parts → Inventory.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: The import finishes without errors.
  • Step 2: Manufacturer still reads [Mfr-1]; Sell Price reads $26.00 (the import did run).

Source — where this behaviour comes from
